questions.question: What will help a company perform a cost benefit analysis of migrating to the AWS Cloud?
questions.explanation: The AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator compares the cost of running a workload on-premises versus on AWS, which is exactly what a cost-benefit analysis of migrating needs. Cost Explorer and Trusted Advisor analyze existing AWS spend, not an on-prem comparison.

questions.question: Which of the following provides the ability to share the cost benefits of Reserved Instances across AWS accounts?
questions.explanation: With consolidated billing in AWS Organizations, unused Reserved Instance discounts in one linked account are automatically applied to matching usage in other accounts. The reporting tools listed only show usage; they don't share RI benefits.

questions.question: A company has multiple AWS accounts and wants to simplify and consolidate its billing process. Which AWS service will achieve this?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations provides consolidated billing, combining all member accounts into one bill (and unlocking volume discounts). Cost Explorer, Budgets, and Cost & Usage Reports analyze costs but don't consolidate billing across accounts.

questions.question: A company is designing an application hosted in a single AWS Region serving end-users spread across the world. The company wants to provide the end-users low latency access to the application data. Which of the following services will help fulfill this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches content at edge locations close to users worldwide, giving low-latency access even when the origin is in a single Region. Route 53 only resolves DNS, and Direct Connect serves a single private site, not global users.

questions.question: Which of the following deployment models enables customers to fully trade their capital IT expenses for operational expenses?
questions.explanation: A fully cloud-based deployment removes owned hardware, turning upfront capital expense (CapEx) into pay-as-you-go operational expense (OpEx). On-premises is all CapEx, and hybrid keeps some CapEx.

questions.question: How is asset management on AWS easier than asset management in a physical data center?
questions.explanation: In the cloud you can reliably inventory every resource programmatically with a few API calls (e.g., AWS Config, EC2 describe calls), which is far easier than physical tracking. AWS does not run discovery scans or auto-generate asset reports on your behalf, so B and C are incorrect.

questions.question: What feature of Amazon RDS helps to create globally redundant databases?
questions.explanation: Cross-Region read replicas place copies of an RDS database in other Regions, providing global redundancy and lower-latency reads. Snapshots, patching, and Provisioned IOPS don't replicate across Regions.

questions.question: Using AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to grant access only to the resources needed to perform a task is a concept known as:
questions.explanation: Granting only the permissions required for a task is the principle of least privilege — a core IAM security best practice.

questions.question: Which methods can be used to identify AWS costs by departments? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Separate accounts per department give each its own bill, and cost allocation tags label resources by department for tracking. MFA, Reserved Instances, and purchase orders don't categorize spend.

questions.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, customer responsibilities include which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Customers are responsible for security IN the cloud — configuring the guest operating system, network, and firewall (security groups). Securing the underlying hardware/facilities and providing compliance documentation are AWS's responsibilities.

questions.question: Which managed AWS service provides real-time guidance on AWS security best practices?
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor inspects your account in real time and gives recommendations across cost, performance, security, fault tolerance, and service limits. X-Ray traces apps, CloudWatch monitors metrics, and Systems Manager handles operations.

questions.question: Which feature adds elasticity to Amazon EC2 instances to handle the changing demand for workloads?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling adds and removes instances automatically as demand changes, providing elasticity. A load balancer distributes traffic but doesn't change capacity.

questions.question: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, customers are responsible for which aspects of security in the cloud? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Customers manage encryption of their data and firewall rules (security groups / network ACLs). Virtualization, hardware, and facilities are AWS's responsibility.

questions.question: Which AWS hybrid storage service enables on-premises applications to seamlessly use AWS Cloud storage through standard file-storage protocols?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises applications to AWS storage using standard protocols (NFS, SMB, iSCSI). Direct Connect is networking, and Snowball is for bulk physical transfer, not ongoing protocol access.

questions.question: What is a responsibility of AWS in the shared responsibility model?
questions.explanation: AWS is responsible for security OF the cloud, which includes the physical hosts and updating their firmware. Patching guest OSes and configuring network ACLs / security groups are customer responsibilities.

questions.question: Which architectural principle is used when deploying an Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) instance in Multiple Availability Zone mode?
questions.explanation: Multi-AZ keeps a standby in another Availability Zone and fails over automatically — an application of the 'design for failure' principle (assume things fail and stay available).

questions.question: What does it mean to grant least privilege to AWS IAM users?
questions.explanation: Least privilege means granting only the permissions required to perform a given task — not broad or administrator access.

questions.question: What is a benefit of loose coupling as a principle of cloud architecture design?
questions.explanation: Loose coupling makes components independent, so the failure of one doesn't cascade and bring down the others.

questions.question: A director has been tasked with investigating hybrid cloud architecture. The company currently accesses AWS over the public internet. Which service will facilitate private hybrid connectivity?
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect provides a dedicated, private network link between an on-premises data center and AWS, replacing public-internet access. NAT Gateway, S3 Transfer Acceleration, and WAF don't provide private hybrid connectivity.

questions.question: A company's web application currently has tight dependencies on underlying components, so when one component fails the entire web application fails. Applying which AWS Cloud design principle will address the current design issue?
questions.explanation: Decoupling components (isolating them so each can keep working if another fails) directly fixes the cascading-failure problem caused by tight coupling.

questions.question: How can a customer increase security to AWS account logons? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication adds a second login factor, and a strong password policy hardens credentials. Certificate Manager, Cognito, and Organizations don't directly secure account logons.

questions.question: What AWS service would be used to centrally manage AWS access across multiple accounts?
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations centrally manages multiple accounts, including service control policies (SCPs) that set guardrails across all of them.

questions.question: Which AWS service can a customer use to set up an alert notification when the account is approaching a particular dollar amount?
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets lets you set cost/usage thresholds and sends alerts when spending approaches or exceeds them. Cost Explorer and Cost & Usage Reports analyze spend but don't alert on thresholds.

questions.question: What can users access from AWS Artifact?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is a self-service portal for on-demand AWS security and compliance documents (e.g., SOC, PCI, ISO reports).

questions.question: Which is the MINIMUM AWS Support plan that provides designated Technical Account Managers?
questions.explanation: A designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) is included only with the Enterprise Support plan.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS Well-Architected Framework design principle related to reliability?
questions.explanation: The reliability pillar emphasizes the ability to recover from failure (and automatically). Single-AZ deployment is the opposite of reliable; cost optimization and operations-as-code belong to other pillars.

questions.question: Which type of AWS storage is ephemeral and is deleted when an instance is stopped or terminated?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 instance store is physically attached to the host and is ephemeral — its data is lost when the instance stops, hibernates, or terminates. EBS, EFS, and S3 persist independently.

questions.question: What is an advantage of using the AWS Cloud over a traditional on-premises solution?
questions.explanation: With on-demand, elastic resources you no longer have to guess future capacity — you scale up or down as needed and pay for what you use.

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS-managed compute service?
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is a fully managed serverless compute service. EC2 requires you to manage instances, and Aurora is a database, not compute.

questions.question: Which of the following is an important architectural principle when designing cloud applications?
questions.explanation: 'Design for failure' is a core cloud principle — assume components fail and build resilience. Storing backups in the same Region, tight coupling, and avoiding multithreading are not recommended practices.

questions.question: Which mechanism allows developers to access AWS services from application code?
questions.explanation: The AWS SDKs are language-specific libraries that let application code call AWS services programmatically. The Console is a UI, and CodePipeline/Config are operational services.

questions.question: Which Amazon EC2 pricing model is the MOST cost efficient for an uninterruptible workload that runs once a year for 24 hours?
questions.explanation: For a short, infrequent, uninterruptible job, On-Demand is cheapest — you pay only for the 24 hours with no commitment. Reserved Instances require a 1–3 year commitment, and Spot can be interrupted.

questions.question: Which of the following services is a MySQL-compatible database that automatically grows storage as needed?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora is MySQL- and PostgreSQL-compatible and automatically grows its storage as data increases. RDS for MySQL needs storage to be provisioned/scaled, and EC2/Lightsail are not managed databases of this type.

questions.question: Which Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) feature enables users to connect two VPCs together?
questions.explanation: VPC peering creates a private network connection between two VPCs. Endpoints connect a VPC to AWS services, and Direct Connect links on-premises to AWS.

questions.question: Which service's PRIMARY purpose is software version control?
questions.explanation: AWS CodeCommit is a managed source-control service hosting private Git repositories. CodeStar manages projects, the CLI is a tool, and Cognito handles user identity.

questions.question: A company is considering migrating its applications to AWS. The company wants to compare the cost of running the workload on-premises to running the equivalent workload on the AWS platform. Which tool can be used to perform this comparison?
questions.explanation: The AWS Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) Calculator compares on-premises costs against the equivalent AWS workload. The Billing console and Cost Explorer report on existing AWS usage only.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a secure, fast, and cost-effective way to migrate or transport exabyte-scale datasets into AWS?
questions.explanation: AWS Snowmobile moves exabyte-scale data using a shipping-container truck. Snowball handles terabyte-to-petabyte scale, not exabyte.

questions.question: Which of the following BEST describe the AWS pricing model? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS pricing is pay-as-you-go and variable — you pay only for what you use, with no fixed-term or planned commitments required.

questions.question: Which load balancer types are available with Elastic Load Balancing (ELB)? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Among the options, Classic Load Balancers and Application Load Balancers are valid ELB types (ELB also offers Network and Gateway load balancers). Third-party appliances like F5/Citrix are not ELB types.

questions.question: Why should a company choose AWS instead of a traditional data center?
questions.explanation: AWS uses a pay-as-you-go model with no long-term contracts, unlike the large upfront commitments of a traditional data center. (Edge locations aren't in every country, and resource quotas do exist.)

questions.question: Which solution provides the FASTEST application response times to frequently accessed data to users in multiple AWS Regions?
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront caches frequently accessed content at edge locations near users, giving the fastest response times globally. CloudTrail and CloudFormation aren't content-delivery services.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a self-service portal for on-demand access to AWS compliance reports?
questions.explanation: AWS Artifact is the self-service portal for on-demand AWS compliance reports and agreements.

questions.question: Which of the following AWS services can be used to run a self-managed database?
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 lets you install and fully self-manage any database engine on the instance. Route 53 (DNS), X-Ray (tracing), and Snowmobile (data transfer) cannot host a database.

questions.question: What exclusive benefit is provided to users with Enterprise Support?
questions.explanation: A designated Technical Account Manager (TAM) is exclusive to Enterprise Support.

questions.question: How can a user protect against AWS service disruptions if a natural disaster affects an entire geographic area?
questions.explanation: Deploying across multiple AWS Regions protects against a disaster that affects an entire geographic area; multiple AZs only protect within one Region.

questions.question: How does AWS MOST effectively reduce computing costs for a growing start-up company?
questions.explanation: On-demand resources let a start-up pay only for peak usage when needed instead of buying for maximum capacity up front.

questions.question: A startup is working on a new application that needs to go to market quickly. The application requirements may need to be adjusted in the near future. Which of the following is a characteristic of the AWS Cloud that would meet this specific need?
questions.explanation: Agility — the ability to provision resources quickly and change direction easily — fits a fast time-to-market with evolving requirements. (Elasticity is about scaling capacity with demand.)

questions.question: Which AWS Support plan provides a full set of AWS Trusted Advisor checks?
questions.explanation: The full set of Trusted Advisor checks is available with the Business and Enterprise Support plans; Basic and Developer get only a limited set.

questions.question: Which of the following services have Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) mitigation features? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: AWS WAF mitigates layer-7 web attacks and Amazon CloudFront absorbs/distributes traffic at the edge with built-in AWS Shield Standard protection. Together they help mitigate DDoS.

questions.question: When building a cloud Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) model, which cost elements should be considered for workloads running on AWS? (Choose three.)
questions.explanation: For workloads on AWS you pay for compute, storage, and data transfer. Facilities and network infrastructure are on-premises costs that the cloud eliminates.
